title: First Contact: Getting Started screenshots (model select + request composer + code snippets)
creator: Lena Rodriguez
description: Create a compact, annotated set of Getting Started screenshots to ship with the next Hosted API docs refresh and the Quickstart guide. Deliverables include: model selector grid (desktop + mobile), interactive request composer screenshots demonstrating temperature/max_tokens/config presets, three language SDK code snippets (curl, python, javascript) with inlined responses, and a small package of light/dark variants and retina exports for docs and the Console. Assets must be ready for embedding in docs pages and the marketing Quickstart modal.
acceptance_criteria: Model selector: single-column mobile and three-column desktop mockups with clear model metadata (name, size, latency badge) and an accessibility-friendly focus state

Request composer: 3 annotated states (empty composer, filled prompt with template variables, streaming response in progress) exported as PNG and SVG, with hotspots for 'temperature', 'max_tokens', and 'model variant'
Code snippets: curl, python, node snippets that match SDK v2 usage patterns, copy-to-clipboard UI shown, and one inline example of streaming using Server-Sent Events or fetch stream
Assets: light and dark themes, 2x retina exports, filenames and alt text provided, and a small README describing intended placement in docs and Console
Handoff: Figma file with frames named per docs section, a GitHub PR stub linking assets, and PM sign-off on final screenshots

designer_notes: Keep the model cards scannable: model name, architecture tag (e.g., Llama-2-7B), latency badge, small cost estimate, and a 'recommended for' microcopy (chat, embeddings, code)
Request composer should demonstrate three presets: 'Quick chat' (low tokens, high temp), 'Precise' (low temp, higher max_tokens), 'Code assist' (structured output + function call hint)
Code snippets must be copy-ready and tested; include inline comments and a small expected-response block below each snippet for docs authors to reference
When exporting, use transparent backgrounds for inline docs images and include a plain PNG crop for the marketing modal
